clue.text: Twice contracting fungal growth in the arm

definitions.note: the definition names a muscle by where it is, the thing found in the arm

indicators.note: contracting means shortening, so the Latin word for twice loses its final letter

parts.note: bis is Latin for twice, the call for a repeat performance
ceps are edible mushrooms, a fungal growth

explanation.surface: Someone twice catches a fungal infection on their arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracting' looks like catching an illness but tells you to cut BIS (Latin 'twice') to BI. The definition is loose: the answer is what lies in the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-headed muscle at the front of the upper limb is located in the arm.

clue.text: Book on famous surgeon's skin problem

parts.note: Joseph Lister was the famous surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A book about a celebrated surgeon's skin condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised bubble of fluid under the skin is a common skin complaint.

definitions.meaning: to kid is to tease, which is to banter or rib someone
rubbish here is worthless husks or refuse

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: to tease playfully is an old verb sense, and husks separated from grain are worthless refuse.

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means to imagine or embellish, so these letters are reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: Capri, for all its fancy reputation, turns out to be ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is the anagram signal working on CAPRISO.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and lacking imagination, an exact synonym for ordinary or everyday.

clue.text: Hunter in Crete cooked a bit of liver

indicators.note: cooked means altered or prepared, so the island's letters are rearranged
a bit of means only a small part, the opening letter, is taken

explanation.surface: On Crete someone cooked a morsel of liver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges CRETE to TERCE; 'a bit of' takes the L of liver.
explanation.definitionFit: A male hawk used in falconry is a bird of prey, a hunter.

parts.note: ex is a Latin preposition meaning without or out of, as in ex dividend
to cite is to quote or produce something as evidence

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble with no proof.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or rouse a reaction is to provoke it.

clue.text: Drink a great deal during musical finale

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a coda is the closing passage of a piece of music
reams means a great deal, as in reams of paper

explanation.surface: Drink plenty during the closing number of a musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fizzy vanilla-flavoured soft drink.

clue.text: Rowdy young woman delayed when holding Edward up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the word for delayed wraps round the name

parts.note: delayed means late

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the short name is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A loud young woman is late because she was holding Edward up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom, so the short name is turned round before 'when holding' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A young woman who behaves in a boisterous, hard-drinking way, British slang.

clue.text: It's distressing to animal's auditory senses

definitions.text: It's distressing to animal's auditory senses

parts.words: It's distressing to animal's auditory senses
parts.note: distressing read as removing tresses, the clipping of a flock; and the phrase animal's auditory senses, said fast, gives the same sound

explanation.surface: Something is painful to an animal's ears.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'distressing' as taking off the tresses of a farm animal, and 'animal's auditory senses' as that animal's hearing; the two run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Clipping the fleece from a woolly farm animal removes its locks, punning on distressing.

parts.note: rig means equipment or tackle, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Australian sports gear arriving in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Latvia.

indicators.note: criminal is used as crooked, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: The police conceal a crook's tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal's' (criminal is) is the anagram signal on POLICEHIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsolete keyed brass musical instrument, forerunner of the tuba.

parts.note: a crook is a shepherd's staff

explanation.surface: A criminal is missing from a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island in the Inner Hebrides, home of Fingal's Cave.

clue.text: I'm in a position to guess

indicators.note: in means the short phrase is placed inside the other word

parts.note: estate means rank or position, as in the three estates
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be well placed to make a guess.
explanation.definitionFit: To guess at a value is to make a rough calculation of it.

clue.text: One carries papers for a quick illustration

parts.note: brief means short or quick
a case is an instance or example, an illustration

explanation.surface: A courier carries documents for a fast picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat bag designed for carrying documents.

clue.text: Bride more prepared to dress up

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked on, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: The bride is made ready more elaborately for the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: To embellish a story or decorate cloth is to dress it up.

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the word for recognises is said out loud

parts.note: recognises means knows

explanation.surface: Someone recognises a strong odour.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell something out is to sniff it, using the organ above the mouth.

parts.note: a cub is a young animal

explanation.surface: A youthful American nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island nation south of Florida.

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
done means made or produced

explanation.surface: A cheat comes up with an excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone wrongdoing is to overlook or excuse it.

clue.text: Producer needs knowledge and time to meet peak

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or knowledge
an era is a period of time
a tor is a rocky hilltop or peak, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A film producer needs know-how and time to reach the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that produces electricity is a producer of power.

indicators.note: houses means contains, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in all bar one

explanation.surface: A pub stocks an unusual choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a pub in the surface but means except.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage selected from a longer work is an extract.

clue.text: Forgot to find glove in dictionary

indicators.note: in means the glove is placed inside the dictionary
this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
a mitt is a glove

explanation.surface: Someone forgot to look up glove in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Left out or neglected is what happens to something forgotten.

parts.note: an imp is a scamp or mischievous child
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A rascal's stage turn leaves a mark on the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The effect something has, the mark it leaves, is its impact.

parts.note: late can mean former, as in the late chairman

explanation.surface: Someone creeps in after time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneak in British school slang is a telltale who informs on others.

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
did means worked or performed

explanation.surface: A man named John worked for one called Frank.
explanation.walkthrough: Both John and Frank look like names; John is a toilet, CAN, and Frank means open.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and open in speech are synonyms.

clue.text: Chemist born during the Christmas period

indicators.note: during means within, so the letter is put inside the season

parts.note: Noel is a word for Christmas

explanation.surface: A pharmacist born at Christmas time.
explanation.walkthrough: Chemist suggests a pharmacist; it is Alfred Nobel, the Swedish chemist who invented dynamite.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Nobel was a Swedish chemist, founder of the prizes.

clue.text: Catholic sect keeps wagon for shoemaker

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the word for sect contains the wagon

parts.note: an order is a religious group, a sect
a wain is a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A Catholic religious order holds onto a cart belonging to a cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a shoemaker, from Cordovan leather.

parts.note: to bat is to hit
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A barrel is struck forcefully.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath is a tub for washing in.

indicators.note: in means the traitor sits inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: Eventually a traitor makes errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is a Latin plural meaning errors, especially in print.

clue.text: Apathetic Triad leader is buried in concrete

indicators.note: buried in means placed inside, so the letter goes into the word for concrete

parts.note: solid means concrete, firm

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The head of a Chinese gang is entombed in concrete.
explanation.walkthrough: Triad is a Chinese criminal gang in the surface; only its leader T is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Unemotional and impassive, close in sense to apathetic.
